claims.explanation: GSK1070916 is a potent, long-residence Aurora B/C inhibitor that kills proliferating cells by disrupting mitosis and cytokinesis, so selectivity is driven by features that increase dependence on Aurora B/C-driven mitotic progression and proliferation rather than by a single lineage. The most consistent pattern is that sensitive lines are highly proliferative and often carry TP53 pathway loss plus oncogenic drivers (KRAS/PIK3CA/EGFR/BRAF/MET/ALK) that sustain mitotic entry, whereas many resistant lines retain intact p53 signaling or are less dependent on Aurora B/C. High AURKB/AURKA expression and loss of p53/CDKN2A are therefore expected to predict sensitivity, while intact p53 and low Aurora kinase expression predict protection.

features.basis: Drug is a potent Aurora B/C inhibitor; target overexpression increases dependence
Aurora kinases are frequently overexpressed/amplified in tumors and drive mitosis
Most selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations, consistent with loss of mitotic checkpoint/apoptosis control
CDKN2A loss in several sensitive lines increases proliferation and mitotic dependence
Oncogenic KRAS in multiple sensitive lines drives proliferation and mitotic entry
PIK3CA mutations enriched in sensitive gastric/esophageal/colorectal lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines NCIH1650 and KYSE70 are among sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma line WM793 is selectively killed
MET-mutant gastric line HGC27 is among most sensitive
ALK-mutant neuroblastoma line KELLY is among most sensitive
ATM mutations appear in several least-affected lines, suggesting reduced sensitivity
STK11-mutant NCIH1623 is among least affected lines
